entries.note: The airline captures the electronic air waybill's data; the goods are not handed over yet. The tracking page has no wording for it.
The pieces are built up for a flight before it departs, so it keeps the stage before it.
A flight manifest records an assignment before the departure, so it keeps the stage before it.
The pieces are unloaded from the flight at the arrival station.
Handed to another airline at a transfer; on a cargo transfer manifest.
Taken over from another airline at a transfer; on a cargo transfer manifest.
The consignee is told the goods can be collected at the arrival station's cargo terminal.
The arrival station receives the waybill's papers, which says nothing about the goods.
The papers are handed to the consignee, often before the goods, so it keeps the stage before it.
The shipment is declared to customs, which neither holds nor releases it.
Customs releases the goods at the terminal; collection follows, so it keeps the stage before it.
The goods move to a customs warehouse; the page gives no outcome.
A count or document mismatch the station records; the goods usually move on, so it keeps the stage before it.
A delivery away from the destination, or of fewer pieces than stated, stays in transit.
